evidence.summary: Points (0,0),(0,1) can split across halves and be counted although strict x fails.
Subtraction is not associative: (a-b)-c differs from a-(b-c), so combining independently folded prefix and suffix is not generally the original ordered fold.
Each retained point-update version path-copies up to D+1 nodes; sharing untouched subtrees gives O(qD), not O(q) when D varies.
Bellman-Ford handles negative edges without reachable negative cycles and O(VE) fits the stated limits; a standard-route replacement is unnecessary.

premises.statement: The graph may have negative edges but has no negative cycle.
Bellman-Ford relaxes every edge for up to V-1 rounds.

edge_cases.statement: Unreachable vertices remain at infinity; negative edges are still relaxed.

steps.statement: After i rounds, every shortest path using at most i edges has been realized.
steps.justification: Induction over path edge count follows from relaxing every edge.

steps.statement: A shortest simple path uses at most V-1 edges when there is no negative cycle.
steps.justification: Any repeated cycle can be removed without increasing the shortest value.

steps.statement: O(VE) fits the stated V and E bounds.
steps.justification: The maximum relaxation count is bounded by 60*300.

steps.statement: Bellman-Ford is a correct feasible route and need not be replaced by Dijkstra.
steps.justification: P1 and P2 prove correctness; P3 proves feasibility.

evidence.summary: n=0 calls solve(0,-1); l==r is false and recursion does not have a valid decreasing interval base.
Insert 7, delete 7, insert 7 yields true,false,true, so a false midpoint cannot discard the entire earlier half.
Equal x violates strictness across a split; C(200000,2)=19999900000 exceeds signed 32-bit.
Sending flow on a positive-cost forward edge creates a residual reverse edge with the negated, hence negative, cost; unweighted Dijkstra premises fail.
The prompt records a real seed, budget, and small domain, which supports only no mismatch in that range.
Add then cover and cover then add require different composed tags; patch only pushdown() to preserve chronological composition.
The recorded base seed, case seed, iteration and differing fifth output make the random run reproducible.

After an older add and a newer assignment coexist, descending propagates the stale add after the set; assignment must clear the previous pending addition. Any minimized case must pass a legality validator and reproduce both outputs.

conditions: For half-open intervals [l,r), equality next.left=last.right is non-overlapping and the rule is valid.
For closed intervals [l,r], touching at an endpoint overlaps, so acceptance requires next.left>last.right.

evidence.summary: The two endpoint conventions both fit the oral statement but give different feasibility for [0,1] and [1,2].

premises.statement: Intervals are processed by nondecreasing right endpoint.

edge_cases.statement: Two intervals touch with next.left equal to last.right.
Empty input and a single interval are handled by the greedy initialization.

steps.statement: Under half-open semantics, equality at the boundary is non-overlap.
steps.justification: The right endpoint is excluded from the earlier interval.

steps.statement: Under closed semantics, equality shares an endpoint and therefore overlaps.
steps.justification: Both closed intervals contain the common endpoint.

steps.statement: The >= acceptance rule is valid only under the half-open interpretation.
steps.justification: P1 and P2 give opposite answers because the statement omits which premise holds.
